content:
Just Eat is giving away a controller with a button dedicated to ordering food.

The 'Stay in the Game' controller features what the food delivery company is calling a 'ChEAT' button under the standard diamond of action buttons. The limited-edition controller is only available through local giveaways in the U.K., and Just Eat has partnered with two local Twitch streamers for the promotion.

"When you’re deep into a high-stakes gaming session, nothing kills the moment faster than having to pause the action just to sort out food," said Tina Koehler, Just Eat's UK&I marketing director. "Just Eat has unlocked the ultimate hack to evade the kitchen, enabling gamers to stay just where they are and locked into play."

The company’s official UK accounts shared an AI-generated rendering of the controller, shown above, with the orange Just Eat feature on an otherwise very familiar looking peripheral. While the announcement doesn't offer any real information about the controller’s design or compatibility, it certainly looks quite a bit like PlayStation's standard DualSense.

Social media has plenty of thoughts about the reveal. While some users think the rendered controller looks surprisingly decent, with one claiming the grips "look better than a stock PS5 controller," others were quick to notice the button’s placement is, well, a little dangerous.

We don’t know how exactly the button works, but it most likely opens an external link to the Just Eat app or website. If it really did let you order food with the literal hit of a button, a couple slip-ups during a GTA car chase could lead to a pile of chicken nuggets at your door and a big dent in your wallet.

We’ll likely learn more when UK-based streamers Angry Ginge and Danny Aarons show off the new controller on Twitch. The two streamers are also how you’ll get your chance to use the controller yourself, as they’ll be sharing giveaway information across their social media accounts. Winners receive the limited-edition controller in addition to £300 in Just Eat credit.

The controller reveal coincides with the launch of GTA 6, as plenty of companies toy with the 'concern' that gamers won’t be able to take their eyes away from Leonida. Just this week, McDonald’s launched its own direct order app in Discord.

The majority of brands, however, have embraced the hype. Popeye’s just launched its own Vice City sandwich, and happens to be a major participant in however this Just Eat controller ends up working.
